newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Hong Kong's Court of Appeal ruled that the Provisional Legislature, installed by China as part of the July 1 handover, was legal. Democratic Party members expressed indignance at the ruling.

-- The southern Chinese city of Shenzhen will take drastic measures to reform state enterprises, including strengthening capital expansion and supporting good quality firms to seek stock market listings and raise capital from the domestic market.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Legal experts said the Court of Appeal's ruling on the legality of the Provisional Legislature could not be treated as a precedent.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Shenzhen will try to get Beijing's approval to introduce joint-venture banks and encourage small- to medium-scale banks from Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. It would also consider letting foreign banks handle yuan currency trading business.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- HSI Services, which compiles the Hang Seng Index of Hong Kong stocks, said it would consider adjusting the criteria for membership in the benchmark indicator if its recent reshuffle of consituents continued to draw criticism from brokers and investors.
-- Boeing said it had not been invited by China Southern Airlines to examine the wreckage of the mainland carrier's aircraft that crash-landed in May with a loss of 35 lives.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Various incentives enjoyed by the business community were to be scrutinised to plug loopholes and contain tax evasion as a long-term strategy to further enhance Hong Kong's competitiveness.
